text:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - Hosted API 503s and high tail latency for text-generation endpoints (customers: 2 enterprise tenants). Alert triggered by >5% 5xx rate and p95 latency >2s for 3+ min. Paging oncall rotation Jon Patel.

Jon Patel: Acked. Oncall looking. Pulling logs now.

Samira Khan: seeing a spike of KV cache misses in the runtime cluster for model-gg-2-small. p95 token generation jumps at ~12:45 UTC. Suspect redis eviction flood during autoscale.

Jon Patel: copying logs -> `curl -s "https://observability/api/queries?range=15m&query=kv_cache_miss_rate" | jq .` shows miss_rate 0.47 at peak.

Priya Rao: I've started a temporary mitigation: turned on per-tenant cache pinning for the two impacted customers and throttled background compaction on that cluster. Requesting a scale-up of the dedicated pool by +2 nodes.

Samira Khan: Good call. Also put a soft-fail fallback to smaller model variant (model-gg-2-quant) for new requests to reduce memory pressure. Command run: 
```
redwoodctl route update --model model-gg-2-small --fallback model-gg-2-quant --policy soft-fail
```

incident-bot: autoscaler action: added 2 nodes to pool rdp-34 in us-west-2 (started 1795506900).

Jon Patel: traffic rerouted away from rdp-34 while nodes boot. Observability shows 503s dropping back under 1% after fallback and scale. p95 latency trending down from 2.7s -> 0.9s.

Luca Moretti: tagging this for affected accounts: AcmeCorp, FinleyHealth. I'll draft a quick proactive note to customers and schedule follow-up.

Maya (support): Please confirm if there was any data exposure or partial responses for customers so I can triage support tickets.

Samira Khan: no evidence of data leakage — errors were timeouts and 5xx. We returned 503s or truncated responses in-flight, but no content persisted outside normal logs.

Priya Rao: handing off to next oncall (Priya) in 30m for degradation watch and cleanup. Handoff notes: mitigations applied, rollback plan is `redwoodctl route rollback --to before-1795506800`, follow postmortem checklist.

Jon Patel: thanks. I'll stay on till the scale-up finishes then drop to watch. :thumbsup:

-- 4 hours later --

Priya Rao: Incident stabilized. Root cause initial hypothesis: Redis eviction storm on cache layer caused high KV miss rates, then cascading latency increased CPU and triggered 503s. We scaled pool +2, enabled fallback model, and pinned caches for impacted tenants.

Samira Khan: Action items I propose: 1) Add eviction-resistant cache tier for hot keys (owner: Samira) 2) Improve autoscaler cooldown + hysteresis for this workload (owner: Priya) 3) Add a synthetic test that simulates cache churn (owner: Eng-ML) 4) Update runbook with explicit fallback policy steps (owner: Jon).

Priya Rao: I'll schedule the post-incident review (PIR). Proposed time: 1795580000 (calendar invite sent) - 60 min. Agenda: timeline, root cause, action items, customer comms.

Luca Moretti: Customer comm plan: status page update now -> incident resolved (postmortem scheduled). RCA to be shared to account contacts by EOD tomorrow. Offer a 1:1 walkthrough and a small credit for impacted windows.

Maya (support): I'll queue support messages to affected tenants and include the status page link + offer for RCA call. Need the initial RCA draft by 17:00 UTC for review.

Samira Khan: I'll draft the technical RCA and include logs, mitigation commands, and suggested long-term remediations. ETA: 15:30 UTC.

Jon Patel: I created a tracking ticket: INC-3987 with the four action items and acceptance criteria. I'll link it to the PIR notes and add estimated timelines.

Priya Rao: Good. Also adding a short-term monitoring rule: alert on sustained kv_cache_miss_rate >0.15 for >2m across any pool (owner: Samira).

incident-bot: Reminder: PIR calendar event at 1795580000 created by Priya Rao.

Luca Moretti: For the customer message, suggested language: 
"We experienced elevated error rates and latency on the Hosted API impacting request reliability for a subset of customers between 12:40-13:20 UTC. Root cause under investigation. We've applied mitigations, service is stable, and we'll share a detailed RCA by tomorrow. We apologize for the disruption and will offer a credit for the impacted period."

Samira Khan: Minor edits: call out model variants impacted and that we enabled fallback; mention no data was exposed.

Maya (support): Adding that to the templated note. Will send to AcmeCorp and FinleyHealth after Samira's RCA draft is attached.

Priya Rao: Postmortem owners: Samira (RCA writeup), Jon (Runbook updates & tracking ticket), Priya (monitoring + autoscaler changes), Eng-ML (synthetic tests). Target: all action items assigned with due dates within 14 days.

Jon Patel: Quick wins: add a metric dashboard tile for kv miss by tenant, and a runbook play to immediately pin caches for top memory tenants. I can knock those out tomorrow morning.

Luca Moretti: I'll reach out to customer success and account execs to coordinate the RCA call once the draft's ready.

Samira Khan: Uploading initial RCA draft to the PIR doc now: https://docs.internal/pir/INC-3987 (will include timeline, logs, mitigations, and long-term plan).

status-bot: Status page updated: Incident resolved. RCA: "Drafting". Next update scheduled for 24 hours.

Priya Rao: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: Samira to deliver RCA draft by 15:30 UTC, Jon to update runbook by Fri EOD, Priya to implement autoscaler cooldown change (staged rollout), Eng-ML to provide synthetic test plan. We'll validate fixes in 2 weeks and close incident once tickets have acceptance criteria met.

Luca Moretti: Noted. I'll prepare customer-facing postmortem email and include proposed credit.

Samira Khan: closing notes: no PII exposure, mitigations reversible, long-term: consider moving hot key tier to nvm-cache in front of redis.

Maya (support): I'll post the status update to the support tickets once Samira's RCA is attached.

incident-bot: Incident closed at 1795509800 (duration ~43m).

Priya Rao: Thread closed for now — reopen if regressions occur. Thanks all. :heart:
